{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"bdfd02186de701281e67d292f9d742008131e80a827a5cfc4fe25eb25843e37d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:87","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Nitrous oxide and altered license penalties, DUI law, implied consent, DUI, extreme DUI and aggravated DUI penalties, ignition interlock devices and the Executive Hearing Office","heading":"C — Nitrous oxide suspensions, altered or fictitious licenses, the DUI law and implied consent, on-the-spot license loss and test refusal, DUI, extreme DUI and aggravated DUI penalties, how a Certified Ignition Interlock Device works, and the Executive Hearing Office","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Nitrous oxide suspensions, altered or fictitious licenses, the DUI law and implied consent, on-the-spot license loss and test refusal, DUI, extreme DUI and aggravated DUI penalties, how a Certified Ignition Interlock Device works, and the Executive Hearing Office
Knowledge domain: the license penalties for using false identification to obtain nitrous oxide and for altered or fictitious licenses, who may not drive impaired, what the Implied Consent Law means, when a driver loses the license on the spot, the refusal penalty, the minimum penalties for DUI, extreme DUI and aggravated DUI, how an ignition interlock device works and who may apply for an interlock restricted license, and what the Executive Hearing Office does.

FACT_ID: sec20-F01 | anchor: A01
Besides the license suspension, the nitrous oxide false-identification offense can also bring fines or a jail sentence. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F02 | anchor: A01
Nitrous oxide, commonly called laughing gas, has legitimate uses such as an anesthetic for doctors and dentists, but it can be habit-forming, and using it over a long time can lead to serious health problems or death. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F03 | anchor: A01
A first nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for 6 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F04 | anchor: A01
A second or later nitrous oxide offense suspends your driving privilege for 12 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F05 | anchor: A01
It is unlawful to display a license you know is canceled, revoked, suspended, fictitious or altered. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F06 | anchor: A01
Altering a license or obtaining a false driver license is illegal and leads to suspension, with possible fines or jail. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F07 | anchor: A01
No one under the influence of alcohol, marijuana, medications or illegal drugs may drive or be in actual physical control of any vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F08 | anchor: A01
By applying for and accepting an Arizona driving privilege, you agree to be tested for alcohol and drugs if you are arrested for DUI, which is called the Implied Consent Law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F09 | anchor: A01
An officer who has reason to believe you drove under the influence will ask you to take a blood, breath, urine or other bodily substance test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F10 | anchor: A01
If a test shows an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more, you lose your driving privilege on the spot. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F11 | anchor: A01
For someone driving a commercial vehicle that requires a commercial driver license, the on-the-spot limit is 0.04. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F12 | anchor: A01
You may be found guilty of driving while intoxicated even when your BAC was below 0.08 percent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F13 | anchor: A01
A driver under 21 may have the license suspended for any alcohol concentration at all. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F14 | anchor: A01
Refusing or failing to complete the tests after a DUI arrest automatically costs you the privilege to drive: 12 months the first time, and 24 months if it is your second refusal in 84 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F15 | anchor: A01
For a second or third DUI offense, the driving privilege is automatically revoked in addition to any criminal penalties from the court. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec20-F16 | anchor: A02
A first DUI offense brings at least 10 consecutive days in jail. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F17 | anchor: A02
A first DUI offense brings a license suspension of at least 90 days and a fine of at least $1,250. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F18 | anchor: A02
A first DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or evidence-based psychotherapy and community service, and the court may order an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F19 | anchor: A02
A second or later DUI offense brings at least 90 days in jail, a fine of at least $3,000 and a 12-month license revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F20 | anchor: A02
A second or later DUI offense also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and community service, and an ignition interlock may be ordered. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F21 | anchor: A02
Extreme DUI applies to a driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or higher. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F22 | anchor: A02
A first extreme DUI brings at least 30 consecutive days in jail and a fine of at least $2,500. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F23 | anchor: A02
On a first extreme DUI with an alcohol concentration of 0.20 or higher, jail is at least 45 days and a suspended sentence is not available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F24 | anchor: A02
A first extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment or psychotherapy, community service, and a Certified Ignition Interlock Device on any vehicle you drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F25 | anchor: A02
A second or later extreme DUI brings a fine of at least $3,250 and a 12-month license revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F26 | anchor: A02
On a second or later extreme DUI at 0.20 or higher, jail is at least 180 days with no suspended sentence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F27 | anchor: A02
A second or later extreme DUI also requires alcohol screening, education or treatment, an ignition interlock and community service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F28 | anchor: A02
Aggravated DUI covers a DUI committed while your privilege is suspended or revoked, a third DUI in 7 years, or a DUI with a person under 15 in the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F29 | anchor: A02
Aggravated DUI also covers a DUI or extreme DUI by a person who is already required to use a Certified Ignition Interlock Device. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F30 | anchor: A02
Aggravated DUI brings prison for not more than 2 years and a 1-year license revocation, on top of any other required penalty. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec20-F31 | anchor: A03
Aggravated DUI also requires alcohol screening, education, treatment or psychotherapy and an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F32 | anchor: A03
A Certified Ignition Interlock Device is a breath alcohol tester wired into the vehicle's ignition and power system. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F33 | anchor: A03
The driver must blow into the interlock before trying to start the engine, and the vehicle will not start if the alcohol level is above a set level. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F34 | anchor: A03
While the vehicle is running, the driver must also blow into the interlock at random intervals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F35 | anchor: A03
For most of the listed DUI-related cases, Arizona law lets a person apply for a Special Ignition Interlock Restricted Driver License on day one of a Class D or Class G suspension or revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F36 | anchor: A03
A person holding an interlock restricted license must follow the interlock rules, finish any required alcohol treatment classes, and carry proof of future financial responsibility coverage. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F37 | anchor: A03
The Executive Hearing Office holds hearings requested by people or businesses contesting an MVD order. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec20-F38 | anchor: A03
Most Executive Hearing Office cases are appeals of an order suspending or revoking a driver license, usually because of traffic law violations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

Misconceptions: a BAC under the legal limit does not guarantee you will not be convicted; refusing a test does not avoid a penalty, since refusal brings its own automatic loss of privilege; extreme DUI is a separate, harsher category starting at a higher alcohol level; aggravated DUI is a prison offense, not just a longer jail term; an interlock must be blown into while driving as well as before starting.
Mnemonics: Point zero eight loses the license, point one five is extreme, point two zero is the top tier; refuse once, lose a year.
Glossary: implied consent means agreeing in advance to alcohol and drug testing by accepting a license; extreme DUI means DUI at a high alcohol concentration; aggravated DUI means a DUI with an aggravating factor such as a suspended license or a passenger under fifteen; ignition interlock means a breath tester that prevents the engine from starting.
Dynamic facts: DUI fines, jail minimums, revocation periods and interlock license eligibility are statutory and change often, so every penalty figure must be rechecked against current Arizona law before release.
